faq.a: Abdoulaye is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ اللَّه, whose core sense is abdoulaye; servant of god (west african form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdoulaye?
faq.a: Abdoulaye is associated with Arabic. Abdoulaye is the West African (Fulani/Wolof) form of Arabic عَبْدُ اللَّه (ʿAbd Allāh), meaning 'servant of God'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ اللَّه is Arabic.
Abdoulaye can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdoulaye should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd Allāh is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdoulaye mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdoulaye is rendered عبداللہ and carries the sense عبداللہ، اللہ کا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdoulaye mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdoulaye is rendered عبدالله and carries the sense عبدالله، بنده خدا.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-dou-laye. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Abdoulaye?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdoulaye, abdoulaye. Script forms are عبدالله, عبداللہ, عَبْدُ اللَّه, अब्दुल्लाहे.
